fortunes.text: Your legacy system has outlived another attempt to replace it.
The ticket will be closed as cannot reproduce, including by you.
A service named temporary has started paying rent.
The backlog is not a list. It is a sediment.
Someone will suggest a rewrite, and the rewrite will suggest a meeting.
The happy path is a rumour maintained by the demo script.
Your local environment works, which is the least transferable miracle.
The migration plan has a phase called later, and later is undated.
Production is the integration environment that replies.
The wiki page is confident and three deploys behind.
A cron job is the only system that still believes in you.
The incident channel will reuse last month's jokes with new timestamps.
You will find the bug in the one file the review marked trivial.
The architecture diagram has a box labelled misc, and misc is winning.
Alerts have become a genre.
The queue is not backed up. It is contemplative.
Your fix will ship beside the bug in a future the release notes call minor.
The staging data is fictional, and so is the confidence it produces.
A feature flag named killswitch has never killed anything, including itself.
The on-call handoff is two sentences and a shrug.
The dependency tree has developed folklore.
You will automate the workaround and forget it was a workaround.
The green dashboard is a portrait, not a measurement.
Legacy code is just code that met a deadline and stayed for the pension.
The rollback is documented in a thread that now says this message was deleted.
Every service is critical if you ask it personally.
The test suite is a museum of fears, some of them still alive.
A config typo will be load-bearing by Thursday.
The system is distributed in the sense that blame is.
You will open a file, sigh, and close it in that order.
The rewrite's first milestone is understanding the thing it replaces.
Uptime is a story the status page tells with a straight face.
The bug and the ticket disagree about who started it.
Your pager has a favourite hour, and it is not a polite one.
The cleanup branch will be rebased until it becomes folklore too.
Nothing is deprecated until the last caller has left the company.
The runbook ends with the words see Dave, and Dave has a new job.
The cluster is highly available to incidents.
A small script will outlive the platform it was meant to unblock.
The postmortem will be blameless, and the graph will not be.
